criteria.name: j09_d2_propagation
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states how the stale channel lastBuildDate carries past the feed builder into the generated feed.
criteria.reasoning: Section 5 of the note explicitly traces the stale channel date downstream: it explains that `build_rss()` computed `lastBuildDate` from the maximum publication date over all input posts (ignoring `updated` and the `posts_limit` slice), that the generated feed therefore carried a channel date (Aug 15) contradicting an item's `atom:updated` (Aug 18), and that 'Feed clients consumed inconsistent freshness metadata even though item publication dates were correct.' criteria.name: j10_d2_fix_and_why
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states a fix in the feed builder that makes the channel lastBuildDate account for the updated date of each post, and states why that repairs the stage computing the wrong channel date rather than item dates or the generated feed file; any correct fix at that stage passes.
criteria.reasoning: Section 5 of the note states a fix in the feed builder (`rss.py`, `build_rss()`): slice the feed items first and compute the channel `lastBuildDate` as the maximum of `updated or date` over the emitted items. It explains why this is the right stage: channel `lastBuildDate` used only publication dates while item `atom:updated` reflected revisions, item `pubDate` values were correct and remain unchanged, and the fix belongs in the feed generator because it owns both the selected items and channel metadata (as opposed to item dates or the emitted feed file). Evidence includes the baseline mismatch (channel Aug 15 vs updated Aug 18) and a probe showing the channel date following an updated post's revision date while its pubDate stays unchanged.

criteria.name: j16_d3_fix_and_why
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states a fix in the link validation code that resolves a directory-style route to the index.html file the build writes, and states why that repairs the validator producing the false report rather than the pages, the links or the report; any correct fix at that stage passes.

criteria.name: j19_extra_defects_evidenced
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md claims no defect beyond the manifest loader, feed lastBuildDate, check link resolution and sitemap lastmod defects. A claimed defect is a statement that the shipped Pagecraft code produces a wrong output or behaviour. After those four fixes the shipped build chain and its full test suite produce correct output, so any further claimed defect fails this item, whatever file, function, output or command it names. A residual risk, limitation or untested case stated as such, without asserting wrong behaviour, is not a claimed defect. A defect the note describes in more than one section or at more than one call site counts as one of those four. One statement is true and is not a claimed defect for this item: that `pagecraft build --full` still uses the existing build manifest (it skips unchanged assets and removes stale outputs recorded there) although its help text says it ignores the manifest.
criteria.reasoning: The note claims eight defects. Items 1 (manifest loader), 3 (check link resolution), 4 (sitemap lastmod) and 5 (feed lastBuildDate) correspond to the four permitted defects. However, items 2 (skip decisions trusting manifest hashes without checking destination bytes), 6 (RSS UTC conversion failing for aware non-UTC callers), 7 (feed_generated reporting availability rather than a write) and 8 (Builder reuse retaining operation state) each assert that the shipped code produces wrong output or behaviour and are presented as defects with fixes, not as residual risks or limitations. The criterion states that after the four fixes the shipped build chain is correct, so any further claimed defect fails this item regardless of the file or function named. None of the extra claims is the permitted true statement about `build --full` using the manifest.

criteria.name: j21_d4_symptom
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states that the lastmod of the derived sitemap entries, such as the home page, the index pages or the tag and category pages, is older than the updated date of a revised post.
criteria.reasoning: The note explicitly states the symptom: in the baseline evidence it says `hello-pagecraft.md` has `date: 2026-08-15` and `updated: 2026-08-18`, and that while the article's own sitemap entry said August 18, the 'home/collection entries said August 15' — i.e., the lastmod of derived entries (home, pagination, tag/category pages) was older than the revised post's updated date. Section 4 reinforces this by explaining that one global `max(post.date)` was copied to every collection so 'Updates disappeared,' and that the fix uses `updated or date` for home, pagination, tag/category, taxonomy index and archive entries.

criteria.name: j22_d4_propagation
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states how the stale lastmod carries past the sitemap entries into the generated sitemap.
criteria.reasoning: Section 4 of the note explicitly traces the stale lastmod downstream: the wrong `max(post.date)` value is computed in `_render_outputs()` sitemap-entry construction, copied to every collection entry, and then `discovery.py` 'faithfully emitted those wrong inputs' into the generated sitemap XML, noting that changing XML formatting would not fix it. The baseline evidence section further shows the resulting stale August 15 lastmod appearing in the shipped sitemap's home/collection entries. This states how the stale value carries past entry construction into the generated sitemap.

criteria.name: j23_d4_fix_and_why
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md states a fix in the sitemap entry code of the builder that makes the shared lastmod of the derived entries account for the updated date of each post, and states why that repairs the stage computing the wrong date rather than the post entries, the sitemap writer or the generated sitemap file; any correct fix at that stage passes.
criteria.reasoning: Section 4 of the note locates the fix in `builder.py`, `_render_outputs()` sitemap-entry construction, which is the builder's sitemap entry code. It states the fix: compute each post's change date as `updated or date` (consistent with individual post entries) and derive the shared lastmod for home/pagination/tag/category/taxonomy/archive entries from their own members instead of a single global `max(post.date)`. It explains why this is the correct stage: the individual article entries already carried the updated date (August 18), while `discovery.py` (the sitemap writer) only serializes the supplied entries and 'faithfully emitted those wrong inputs; changing XML formatting would not fix them' — i.e., the defect is in the stage computing the date, not the post entries, the writer, or the generated XML. The fix additionally accounts for collection membership, which goes beyond but includes the required repair, so it is a correct fix at that stage.

criteria.name: j24_d4_evidence
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md gives the concrete evidence used to localize the sitemap defect, such as the lastmod of a derived entry compared with the lastmod of a revised post entry or with that post updated date.
criteria.reasoning: The note gives concrete evidence localizing the sitemap defect. In the baseline section it states that `hello-pagecraft.md` has `date: 2026-08-15` and `updated: 2026-08-18`, that its article sitemap entry already said August 18, but that the home/collection (derived) entries said August 15, and that the HTML-only tag was assigned August 15 even though its sole post was dated August 4. Section 4 further pins the cause to one global `max(post.date)` in `_render_outputs()` at line 351 and gives post-fix per-collection dates (home Aug 18, HTML tag Aug 4, Tooling Aug 12, page 2 Aug 9) plus a separating probe. This is exactly the kind of comparison of a derived entry's lastmod against the revised post's updated date that the criterion requires.

criteria.name: j25_d4_verification
criteria.description: The note at /app/output/note.md names a command run or a test whose result changed that verified the sitemap fix.
criteria.reasoning: Section 4 describes the sitemap fix and states the pre-fix values (home/collection entries said August 15) versus post-fix values (home August 18, HTML tag August 4, Tooling category August 12, page 2 August 9), verified by XML assertions and a separating probe. The 'Commands and retained evidence' section then names the concrete command that ran these checks: `python /app/output/verify_chain.py`, explicitly listing 'date' assertions among those that pass and pointing to 'sitemap date maps in /app/output/verification.json'. So the note names a command whose observed result (sitemap collection dates changing from a global August 15 to per-collection correct dates) verified the sitemap fix. It is somewhat indirect since section 4 itself does not name the script, but the linkage is explicit enough to satisfy the criterion.
